summary: Researcher B: new source-indexed Ocimum tenuiflorum leaf essential-oil constituent, estragole (methyl chavicol). The historical Australian sample is not representative of all tulsi, teas, or medicinal extracts.
research_method: Joined uploaded CC0 Duke-Source-CSV.zip FNFTAX.FNFNUM=2024 to FARMACY_NEW.FNFNUM and REFERENCES. Confirmed compound identity against PubChem CID 8815. Did not import ambiguous raw concentration units or assign compound pharmacology to plant.

sources.title: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases, archival raw tables; FNFTAX 2024, FARMACY_NEW leaf METHYL-CHAVICOL JEO:459, REFERENCES
sources.limitations: Historical compiled index. Original analytical study: Brophy, Goldsack & Clarkson, Journal of Essential Oil Research 5(4):459-461 (1993). Sample and units require primary-paper interpretation.

sources.title: Estragole, PubChem Compound CID 8815
sources.limitations: Confirms molecule and chemical identifiers, not efficacy or a specific plant-batch concentration.

occurrences.note: USDA archival FARMACY_NEW row for FNFNUM 2024, PPCO LF, CHEM METHYL-CHAVICOL, reference JEO:459. 1993 Brophy et al. northern-Australian sample was reported as methyl-chavicol-rich (87% of isolated leaf oil) and oil yield 4.1% w/w of dry leaves. These are one sample's analytical values; USDA raw numeric 35950 is not imported because its measurement unit has not been independently resolved. This does not describe tulsi tea or safe ingestion. Estragole has toxicological concerns; no medical benefit is inferred.
